$comment: npm scopes that are dependency-confusion targets: an organization's private scope that an attacker registered on the public registry. The malicious versions are the attacker's, the NAME is the victim's own internal package, so a whole-package verdict in one of these scopes is settled into exact pins and never becomes a bare name (which would flag every developer installing the real package from the private registry). A record that yields no version stays an unmapped gap and belongs in threat-feed-unresolvable.json. See docs/threat-feed-sources.md, section 'Pin-only scopes'.

scopes.reason: Dependency-confusion squats of a company's internal scope (MAL-2026-17249 to MAL-2026-17282, 2026-09-28), published at internal-looking versions such as 1.99.0 and 40.14.3. The real packages live in the victim's private registry.

Dependency-confusion squats of a company's internal scope at sentinel versions 99.x (MAL-2026-11196, MAL-2026-13436, MAL-2026-17204, MAL-2026-17205). The real packages live in the victim's private registry.

Dependency-confusion squats at sentinel versions 999.0.x whose postinstall hook exfiltrates host and credential data (MAL-2026-17688 to MAL-2026-17691, 2026-10-08). The real packages live in the victim's private registry.
Dependency-confusion squat at sentinel versions 999.0.0 to 999.0.4 published 2026-05-13 (MAL-2026-3653). The real package lives in the victim's private registry.
